content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity) — Section 4.2(a) Termination Payment.**

What I found:

- **Notice mechanics are acceptable (fallback).** Section 4.1 (p0024) sets a one-year term auto-renewing annually, terminable by *either* Party on 90 days' written notice. Our 90-day exit sits inside the 60–90 day fallback band, and HDI's mirror right effectively operates only at an anniversary on 90 days' notice — so there is no short-notice vendor walk-away mid-term. No redline needed here.
- **The exit fee fails the fallback.** Section 4.2(a) (p0026) makes *any* Company termination trigger a payment of 50% of the prior twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000, payable in eight quarterly instalments (p0029). Fees under Section 3.1 are 30% of monthly Net Sales over $11,000, so on ~$2M of annual Net Sales the exit payment would be roughly four times the fallback ceiling of three months' fees — and it is uncapped as Net Sales grow. On its face it also bites where we terminate for HDI's breach; Section 1.6's "without penalty" carve-out covers only late go-live.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`): capped the Termination Payment at the lesser of the existing formula and three months' Section 3.1 fees, tied it to convenience terminations under Section 4.1, and disapplied it where we exit for HDI's breach or non-performance.

I pitched this at the **fallback** rather than deleting the payment outright, because HDI's site build and hosting are compensated solely through revenue share, making a total penalty deletion disproportionate to the existing bargain. If HDI resists, the preferred position (convenience exit without penalty) remains available as our push.
